summary: A slide deck from the WR Meetup #13 (7 Oct 2021) by Bence Magyar and Denis Štogl introducing ros2_control, a robot-agnostic control framework for ROS2. It covers why a control framework is needed, the history from pr2_controller_manager through ros_control to ros2_control, the shortcomings of ros(1)_control, the ros2_control architecture ("everything is an interface"), the URDF <ros2_control> tag, lifecycle, real-world use cases, and code examples for a system hardware interface and forwarding controllers using the RRBot example.
one_line: Slide deck introducing ros2_control, a robot-agnostic ROS2 control framework, comparing it with ros_control and showing URDF tags and code examples.
key_facts: The talk is WR Meetup #13 held on 7 Oct. 2021 and is titled "ros2_control - a robot-agnostic control framework for ROS2".
Bence Magyar is a PhD in Robotics, Lead Software Engineer at FiveAI, and a ros_control and ros2_control maintainer.
Denis Štogl is a Control Engineer and Roboticist, Robotics Consultant at Stogl Robotics Consulting, and a ros2_control maintainer.
The history timeline lists pr2_controller_manager (pr2_mechanism) in 2009, ros_control in 2012/2013, and ros2_control in 2017/2021.
In ros(1)_control, joint interfaces were limited to "position", "velocity", and "effort".
In ros2_control, interface types are strings, making them fully flexible, and the framework distinguishes Actuator, Sensor, and System hardware types.
ros2_control provides a default "ros2_control_node", removing the need to implement a control node for each hardware.
Hardware interfaces in ros2_control are always plugins with a lifecycle, so a robot cell can be created via plug-and-play.
Standard interface names in ros2_control are "position", "velocity", "acceleration", and "effort".
In the URDF <ros2_control> tag, <hardware> defines the plugin and its parameters, <joint> describes 1 DoF, <sensor> covers sensing not related to a joint, and <gpio> covers everything else.
The slides state that all interfaces internally have type double.

To use ros2_control, one writes the <ros2_control> tag (tip: as a xacro macro), implements a hardware interface (Actuator for 1 DoF motors, Sensor for sensors, System for multi-DoF robots), and configures controllers and the controller manager.
The UR driver is described as the first open-source driver with ros2_control integration.
The Dynamixel use case (youtalk/dynamixel_control) uses multiple servos and is a reference implementation for ROBOTIS OpenManipulator-X.
The RRBot example's test command publishes to /rrbot_controller/commands with joint displacements of 0.5 and 0.5 for two joints.
The references include the ros_control paper in the Journal of Open Source Software and the site https://control.ros.org.
